children.translated_text: May <s>Sanmati</s>, who pierced people's inner darkness with the sun of true knowledge,

children.text: yaḥ sanmatitvam āpannaḥ sanmatiḥ sanmatiṃ kriyāt ||
children.translated_text: and who attained the state of right understanding, bring about right understanding.
I praise <s>Vṛṣabha</s>, the eminent bull, whose emblem is the bull and who is worshipped by the eminent,
the founder of the excellent <s>tīrtha</s> (ford of liberation) and destroyer of the enemies that are karmas.
For the attainment of the supreme station reached by those who have attained the rank of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
I bow to the two feet of the <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, who is truth itself.
The venerable speech of the <s>Arhats</s> is a lamp illuminating the world and what lies beyond it;

children.text: rajo vidhūya no nityaṃ tanotu vimalām matim ||
children.translated_text: may it always dispel our dust of passion and extend to us a stainless understanding.
May those venerable feet that bring one's desired aims to accomplishment,
the feet honored for their good conduct, be boats for me across the ocean of existence.
Though lacking ability, I shall speak, impelled by devotion to my teachers,
of the glorious deeds of <s>Bhadrabāhu</s>, as I learned them from my teacher's words.
When this account is heard, it shakes away the vast darkness of false delusion from the simple-minded
and produces stainless understanding upon the pure Jain path.
Now, here in the region called <s>Magadha</s>, in the land of <s>Bhārata</s>,
the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> shines like the city of <s>Purandara</s>.
Its protector was <s>Śreṇika</s>, before whom the entire succession of kings bowed, a benevolent repository of excellence;
his sovereign chief queen was <s>Celanī</s>.
One day that lord of the people learned from a forest keeper
that <s>Mahāvīra</s>'s <s>samavasaraṇa</s> (universal preaching assembly) had arrived at Mount <s>Vipula</s>.
Filled with supreme joy and wishing to bow to the Lord, he set out,
while the magnificent sound of the threefold musical performance deafened every quarter.
He beheld the one attended by gods, radiant with the brilliant splendor of omniscience;
after praising, bowing to, and fully worshipping him, the king stood in the assembly of men.
With humility he listened to the twofold <s>dharma</s> proclaimed by the <s>Jina</s>;
then, bowing down and joining his hands like a flower bud, the king asked:
"O Lord, in this declining age, how many teachers of omniscience and scripture

children.text: kiyanto 'gre bhaviṣyanti kiṃ kiṃ cāto bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will arise hereafter, and what events will then occur?"

children.text: śrutvā tadīyaṃ vyavahāraṃ vyājahāra girāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard his question, the Lord of Speech replied
in tones like the deep rumbling of thunderclouds, delighting the peacocks that were souls capable of liberation:

children.text: mayi muktim ite rājan gautamākhyaḥ sudharmavāk
children.translated_text: "When I have attained liberation, O king, there will be one named <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Sudharman</s>,
and one named <s>Jambū</s>; these three will possess the vision of omniscience."
